title: Claude's 20% boost is back, and this time we're celebrating Opus 5.5
excerpt: Longer sessions meet faster, cheaper outputs as Opus 5.5 reduces token use and speeds up professional workflows.
content_html:
Published Sep 23, 2026, 7:35 AM EDT

Hamed holds a B.A. in English Literature, graduating cum laude. He loves music, tech gadgets, and exploring the latest in the world of LLMs. He also enjoys tinkering with creative software such as Logic Pro, Final Cut Pro, and Photoshop.

A lifelong musician, Hamed plays multiple instruments, including guitar, bass, and oud. He is equally fascinated by smart-home technology and can happily spend hours geeking out over connected lights, speakers, sensors, and automations that make everyday life a little more interesting. When he isn’t covering the latest tech news, he explores more creative topics on his Medium blog, works on his music, or clears his head by riding his motorcycle.

Summary

  • Claude's five-hour usage cap raised 20% for Pro/Max/Team, plus a rain-day rate-limit reset.
  • Opus 5.5 matches Fable 5.1 on most tasks, costs ~40% less than Opus 5, and uses fewer tokens.
  • More headroom plus Opus 5.5's efficiency stretches sessions for big coding projects.

Claude users, rejoice: Anthropic has increased Claude's five-hour usage limits by 20% for Pro, Max, and Team subscribers. The company is also giving subscribers a rate-limit reset to use on a rainy day.

The extra headroom comes alongside Claude Opus 5.5. According to Anthropic, Opus 5.5 can deliver performance on par with Fable 5.1 on most tasks while costing about 40% less than Opus 5.

An Anthropic model launch worth celebrating

More Claude before cooldown is better than benchmark-breakers with limitations

Arguably, the most frustrating thing about using Claude is hitting the usage limits. Somehow, it always seems to happen when you are right in the midst of a flow state, forcing you to leave your project unfinished for the next five hours or spend money on tokens. While a 20% increase won't eliminate that ceiling altogether, it should make it noticeably harder to hit during ordinary work.

Anthropic says Opus 5.5 costs $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, both 20% below Opus 5. Not only that, but it also uses fewer tokens to finish a task, produces output 30% faster, and cuts cache-read pricing by 60%. The combination of a larger allowance and the model's improved efficiency should stretch each session considerably further.

If you've watched Claude Code devour a usage allowance, you know exactly why this is welcome. The problem got so bad that we often had to cut corners and develop strategies to reduce Claude Code usage billing —and we managed to do that by 40%. While those tactics remain useful, it's good to know that you don't have to aggressively optimize every prompt just to finish a project.

Opus 5.5 is also aimed squarely at those larger projects. Anthropic says it leads its previous models in agentic coding, computer use, and professional knowledge work. Based on Anthropic's documentation, one early tester completed a 680,000-line code migration in less than a day, while another tester audited and repaired a 200,000-line codebase in under three hours.

These claims sound more convincing after seeing someone use Claude to build an entire operating system from scratch that runs DOOM. That project required many back-and-forth sessions, along with extensive testing and troubleshooting with Claude — the exact kind of work that benefits from more room before the limit arrives.

Opus 5.5 is now available to Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise customers, while Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 are due in the coming weeks.
